# Fieldnote Clinic Pilot: One-Page Summary

## Trial and reach
From 1 September to 15 November, Fieldnote’s offline notes app was tested in Pune, Nagpur and Nashik. Nurses used shared tablets on home visits and synced notes when back on clinic Wi-Fi. The pilot recorded 412 visits: 168 in Pune, 139 in Nagpur and 105 in Nashik.

## Results
The median sync time was 38 seconds. Some syncs in Nashik took as long as four minutes because its Wi-Fi dropped several times a day. No notes were lost, and tablets lasted a full shift at all three clinics. Nurses gave the app an average rating of 4.3/5. The visit template was the most valued feature, reducing write-up time from about nine minutes to five. Photo upload was the least liked, described as slow and confusing.

Two incidents occurred. On 22 September, two tablets editing the same visit offline created a duplicate patient record in Nagpur; staff merged it manually that day. On 14 October, an expired sync-server certificate caused a three-hour outage. Neither incident harmed a patient.

## Spending
The pilot used ₹18.5 lakh of its ₹22 lakh budget, leaving ₹3.5 lakh for the next phase. Costs were ₹9 lakh for tablets, ₹4 lakh for training, ₹3.5 lakh for support and ₹2 lakh for the sync server.

## Clinic requests and next steps
Clinic leads requested simpler photo uploads, a warning when multiple tablets edit the same visit, and printed visit summaries for patients without phones. Nashik also requested queued syncs that wait for stable Wi-Fi.

The team recommends expanding to 10 clinics in March, after simplifying photo upload and adding the edit-conflict warning. It also recommends monitoring certificate expiry immediately. A second review is planned for June.
